context:
Goal: know when a live price should change, without noise.
Problem (money): drift costs sales on cards priced over market; how loud the alert is decides what you act on.
Based on (measured): the count over your 832 live listings below.
Drift helps one decision: should this live price change now? A count over your 832 live listings with a market price:
- 7 are more than 10% under market. Together they lose $0.46.
- 444 are more than 10% over market, $3,124 in all.
- 11 cards are each $5 or more over market, and hold $2,845.
So drift never costs money by selling too cheap. It costs sales by pricing over what buyers pay, and it sits in 11 cards. The count cannot tell which of those you hold high on purpose.
This also answers whether the price-movers block goes: options 1 and 2 remove it, and its read becomes the market-moved rows (list mockup notes, point 10).

options.gain: Nothing new to learn; the 11 cards show first.
options.how: The one pricing list carries it: an over-market listing shows as a suggested cut, and a high-value one lands on top in Needs you.
options.label: Cut drift as a separate tool
options.lose: You see drift only when you open Pricing.

options.gain: You see it without opening Pricing.
options.how: As above, and Home says e.g. '11 listings priced $2,845 over market' with one press to them, only when a high-value card is past the limit.
options.label: One list plus a Home line

options.how: Only cards above the value line are watched on the daily price refresh; each crossing names the card.
options.label: Expensive-card watch
options.lose: A new alert surface; cheap cards wait for the list.

title: What should drift alerts do?
why: The measured cost is 11 cards, and the one list already puts those on top. A separate alert would repeat it.
